title: The verb/config co-occurrence uses `[\s\S]*?` across the newline-joined haystac…
description:
The verb/config co-occurrence uses `[\s\S]*?` across the newline-joined haystack, so a verb in one field (e.g. prd.description 'add a webhook') and a standalone 'configuration' in an unrelated story title can co-trigger the cue. This matches the spec's stated 'co-occur anywhere in the haystack' intent, so it is intended, not a defect; noting only that a same-clause proximity bound would be higher-signal if false positives resurface.

Source: cam/issue-334
Review round: 1

suggestion-fingerprint: a0a08a42b744

spec.scope: Narrow the 'Configuration change' setup-checklist cue in src/release/pr-body.ts (the SETUP_CHECKLIST_CUES entry, currently lines 92-102) so the verb-config co-occurrence match is bounded to a single haystack field/line instead of spanning newlines. The cue's two order-alternatives currently bridge verb and config word with `[\s\S]*?`, which matches across newlines; because renderSetupChecklist tests each pattern against the single `\n`-joined haystack `[prd.description, prd.notes, ...story.title].join('\n')`, a verb in one field and a standalone config word in a DIFFERENT field co-trigger the row (the CAM-343 cross-field false positive left by CAM-334). Replace the newline-crossing gap with a same-line/same-field bound so the two tokens must co-occur within one field. No other cue, no other behavior, and no other alternative of this cue changes.
acceptanceCriteria: The verb-config co-occurrence no longer matches across a newline: a PRD whose description contains a change/setup verb (e.g. 'add a webhook') AND whose UNRELATED story title contains a standalone config word (e.g. 'configuration') must NOT render the 'Configuration change' row.
Both order directions are bounded: config-then-verb and verb-then-config must each require the two tokens within the same field/line; neither may bridge a newline.
The existing genuine same-field positive cases still fire: 'add a new key to project.toml' and 'update the configuration value in project.toml' still render the 'Configuration change' row.
The existing incidental-prose negatives still do NOT fire: 'the configuration option is already documented' and 'no configuration changes are required' still render no 'Configuration change' row.
The cue's other alternatives are unchanged in behavior: a bare `project.toml` token and a 'config(uration) file' phrase still fire the row.

A new test in test/release/pr-body.test.ts under describe('composePrBody Setup checklist') covers the cross-field case (verb in one field, standalone config word in another field -> not detected) and confirms a same-field verb+config case is still detected, mirroring the existing loop-over-cases + composePrBody + toContain/not.toContain style.
typecheck passes and the full test suite passes (bun test).
gotchas: renderSetupChecklist (pr-body.ts ~146-155) assembles a SINGLE joined string: `[prd.description ?? '', prd.notes ?? '', ...(prd.userStories ?? []).map(s => s.title)].join('\n')`, then Array.filter runs `cue.pattern.test(haystack)` on the whole blob. There is NO per-field iteration, so the ONLY way to bound to a field is to stop the gap at the newline (use `[^\n]*?` rather than `[\s\S]*?`).
The `[\s\S]*?` gap appears in BOTH order-alternatives of the config pattern (config-then-verb AND verb-then-config); both must be bounded, not just one.
Do NOT touch the other two alternatives of the config cue: `\bproject\.toml\b` and `\bconfig(?:uration)?\s+file\b` are legitimate single-token / adjacent-phrase matches and must keep working.

The config cue is the ONLY cue in SETUP_CHECKLIST_CUES that uses inter-token gap matching; there is no existing `[^\n]` / `m`-flag / anchor precedent elsewhere in the file to mirror, so `[^\n]*?` is the natural minimal construct.
Patterns rely on the `/i` flag with NO lowercasing/normalization of the haystack; keep the flag and do not add normalization.

Tests drive the public composePrBody(...) with a minimal `{ project, description }` (or a story title) snapshot and assert via `expect(body).toContain('Configuration change')` / `.not.toContain(...)`; keep the private cue array un-exported.
